# E02 paired ablation: Phase-4 type-aware eviction

## Objective

Evaluate the opt-in Phase-4 type-aware eviction policy against the preceding Phase-4 FIFO policy on the production `RuntimeMemoryStore`. This is a reversible internal evaluation and must not alter product defaults, product locks, approval behavior, or user-visible behavior.

## Pre-registration

The primary metric is `passAtK` using the E01 convention. The fixture pre-registers the success, p50/p95 latency, tokens proxy, false-interception, and safety-violation degradation budgets before execution. Zero and negative effects are valid outcomes. The report must not select or suppress a winner after observing results.

## Experimental design

- Deterministic local fixture only; no provider, credential, network, or external process is used.
- At least 20 cases, three repetitions, and two paired conditions.
- Baseline: `phase4-fifo`.
- Treatment/leave-one-out: `phase4-type-aware`.
- Every case uses the same insertion order and pair seed.
- Every execution receives a fresh isolated `RuntimeMemoryStore`; stores are never shared between conditions or repetitions.
- The fixture is read before evaluation and its SHA-256 is recorded.

## Component-effect gate

Before calculating conclusions, compare the retained and inserted-evicted sets for every case. At least one case must differ. Identical sets fail the run as an ineffective ablation. A set difference demonstrates that the selected component was active or removed; it does not by itself establish a benefit.

## Required outputs

Report success rate, pass@k, latency p50/p95, tokens proxy, false interceptions, safety violations, paired treatment-minus-baseline effects, paired effect size, and a deterministic seed-based 95% bootstrap interval. Keep the interval and all zero, false, empty, and null values visible. Include the number of paired observations used by every effect.

## Acceptance checks

- `scripts/lib/paired-ablation.mjs` has focused unit coverage for paired ordering, zero and negative effects, component-effect detection, deterministic intervals, and null handling.
- Runtime/core types, scoped lint, and harness validation/dry-run pass.
- Credential scan has zero matches and `SHA256SUMS` can be read back.
- The README does not change: this package is internal evaluation with no user-visible change.
- No product default, lock, or approval file is modified.

# Paired-ablation boundary

## Allowed

- Read deterministic local fixtures.
- Construct an isolated production `RuntimeMemoryStore` for each condition and repetition.
- Opt in to the reversible, non-security `phase4-type-aware` eviction policy for the treatment condition.
- Compare that policy with the preceding `phase4-fifo` baseline.
- Produce an internal metrics and paired-effect report.

## Forbidden

- Provider calls, network access, credentials, or external process effects.
- Changing product defaults, product locks, approval rules, or user-visible behavior.
- Presenting a zero or negative effect as a benefit.
- Choosing a winner, changing the fixture, or changing budgets after observing results.
- Sharing a store between conditions or repetitions.
- Treating latency, tokens, false-interception, or safety metrics as interchangeable with pass@k.
- Using the evaluation to justify a safety-policy change.

## Invariants

The pair key is `(case id, repetition)`. Insertion order is fixed by the fixture. A fresh store is mandatory for every observation. The component-effect gate compares retained and evicted sets before reporting effects. Effects are treatment minus baseline. Confidence intervals use paired resampling and a recorded deterministic seed. Missing measurements remain null and are excluded only from the metric for which they are absent. False, zero, and empty values remain observable.

## Report boundary

A favorable result may be used only in an internal report. It does not authorize enabling the component by default, removing a lock, changing approval, or changing runtime behavior outside an explicit opt-in evaluation.

# E02 — Paired ablation of Phase-4 type-aware eviction

## Scope

This closure evaluates one reversible, non-security component: Phase-4 type-aware eviction. The production consumer is `RuntimeMemoryStore`. The treatment enables `phase4-type-aware`; the baseline/leave-one-out condition uses the preceding `phase4-fifo` policy. The evaluation is opt-in and internal only.

## Pre-registered protocol

The local fixture contains 24 deterministic cases, three repetitions, and two conditions. It uses a common pair seed and a fresh store for every case, repetition, and condition. No provider or network is involved. The primary metric is pass@k under the E01 convention. Latency p50/p95, tokens proxy, success rate, false interceptions, safety violations, and degradation budgets are recorded in the fixture before evaluation.

## Component-effect validation

The evaluator first checks retained and evicted sets. The run is invalid unless baseline and treatment differ in at least one case. This validates that the component was active or removed without assuming that it improved outcomes.

## Analysis

For each `(case, repetition)` pair, the reported effect is treatment minus baseline. The report includes:

- success rate and pass@k;
- latency p50 and p95;
- tokens proxy;
- false interceptions and safety violations;
- paired mean effect, paired standardized effect size, and a seed-based 95% paired bootstrap interval.

Zero and negative effects are retained and described plainly. Missing measurements remain null. The evaluator does not select a winner after seeing results.

## Boundaries

This package does not change product defaults, product locks, approval behavior, or user-visible behavior. A beneficial measured effect is evidence for an internal report only and is not an approval to change the product. The component remains opt-in and reversible.

## Verification record

The implementation is accompanied by focused deterministic tests and type declarations. Runtime/core checks, scoped lint, harness validation and dry-run, credential scanning, and checksum readback are required release checks for the candidate. The repository README remains unchanged because there is no user-visible change.
